breaking.change: A style pack's `fonts` is a list of font files (`"fonts": ["Body.ttf", "@styles/shared/Cinzel[wght].ttf"]`). A file's family, weight, style and width are the file's own, and `theme.fontFamily` names the families as the files name them, in order: a later family in a list draws the characters an earlier one lacks. A face's `family`, `weight`, `style` and `unicodeRange` are removed with no replacement. Lost: one alias family over several files (Cartoon Label, Scifi Label, Fantasy Caps), a weight range narrower than the file's (a label family held at 600 to 700), and a range that kept a face to some characters (a CJK face now also draws any other character the families before it lack).
breaking.fix: Write each face as its file's path and name the files' own families in `theme.fontFamily`: `"sans": "\"Barlow Semi Condensed\", \"Chakra Petch\", \"Noto Sans SC\""`. The cook refuses a `fonts` entry that is still an object and says so.

breaking.change: `UiDesc.font`, `displayFont`, `monoFont` and `roundedFont` set the theme's fonts: each puts its font's family first in its role's CSS family list (`font-sans`, `font-display`, `font-mono`, `font-rounded`), ahead of the style pack's families. A role's fallback is that list and nothing built in: display and mono end with the sans list, rounded with the display list. Before, a role with no font took a fixed chain (rounded, display, body) of whole fonts; now each character takes the first family of the list that has it.
breaking.fix: None needed where a role's font has every character its texts show. To keep a role in one face, give that role its font.

breaking.change: TSX text is laid out once by Parley from the font files and drawn as glyph coverage at its drawn size on whole device pixels, not from cooked distance-field atlases. A line sits by CSS's half-leading with its baseline on a pixel, so labels move down by 1 to 3 px at 12 to 20 px (more at large sizes) to where a browser draws them, and small text is lighter. `font-bold`, `italic`, `font-display`, `font-mono` and a pack's families now pick real faces and weights (weight 600 and up was a 3 % thickening of the body face); bold or italic the family has no face for is synthesised. Text measures with kerning and shaping, so boxes sized to their text change by up to a few px. `truncate` and `text-ellipsis` end a cut line in "…"; `text-center` and `text-right` align wrapped lines; `tabular-nums`, `oldstyle-nums` and `small-caps` ask the font for those forms, and digits are proportional unless `tabular-nums` asks. A text outline (`text-stroke-*`) is the stroked outline at its full width, and a text shadow a blur of the glyphs. A text with no line height set anywhere above it takes CSS's `normal`, its fonts' ascent and descent, where it took 1.2 of its size (a style pack's type steps set one, so this shows in a UI with no pack classes on its text). A font with an optical size axis (`opsz`, as fantasy's Newsreader) draws at its size's design, as CSS's `font-optical-sizing: auto` does: small text is wider and sturdier, large text finer. `UiDesc.textScale` scales every TSX text's size, line height and spacing, and its box follows.
breaking.fix: Capture the game's screens again and look at them; add `tabular-nums` to timers, scores and counters whose digits must not shift.

breaking.change: A font ships its whole file, and TSX text draws every character the file has: an import's `charset` no longer limits what a TSX label draws from that font. The missing-glyph warning for TSX text names a character only when no font of the UI has it, and no longer names a face or its charset. A cooked game carries each font at its file's size. Text queued with og.render.text and floating text still read the cooked atlas and its charset.
breaking.fix: None needed where the charset only cut the atlas. A game that used `charset` to keep a face from drawing some characters lists another family first in the role's family list, or ships a font file without them.

added.summary: `break-words` (`wrap-break-word`), `wrap-anywhere` and `break-normal` (`wrap-normal`) set CSS `overflow-wrap` on TSX text: under `break-words` a word wider than its box breaks at the box's edge while the other words wrap whole, and a box sized to its content still keeps its longest word; under `wrap-anywhere` it may shrink to a letter.

fixed.summary: A character none of a text's families has is drawn from the game's `fallbackFonts`, the style pack's files, the locale's fonts and font packs, then the default face, so Chinese under a pack draws with no `fallbackFonts`; one no font has is named once in a warning and draws nothing, never a box.
An `Input`'s caret stands where the shaped text puts it (after kerning, ligatures and right-to-left runs), on the line that holds it.
